On Qualcomm devices, hotspot traffic can be fast-pathed in hardware straight to the mobile/Wi‑Fi uplink, skipping iptables entirely — this is why VPN sharing can fail with every VPN app, not just this one. Full mode now auto-detects this (see the Logs tab) and, when you turn this on, stops the daemon behind it and restarts it when you stop sharing. On some devices that same daemon also carries the phone\'s own mobile data, so stopping it can briefly interrupt your own connection while sharing is on — Full mode checks for that and puts it back automatically if it happens, but only turn this on if plain Full mode\'s routing looks correct while no traffic actually goes through.

Instead of turning on the phone\'s hotspot by hand, VPSH creates its own Wi‑Fi access point with the name and password below and shares it through the tunnel automatically. Needs root and Android 11+; if it can\'t be created, VPSH falls back to detecting a hotspot you turned on manually.

Creating a named access point automatically needs root — this is an Android restriction on setting a custom Wi‑Fi name/password from an app, not a limitation of VPSH. Without root, turn on the phone\'s hotspot yourself below and use Proxy mode.

Not available on this device: creating a named access point uses an Android system command that only exists on Android 11 and up. Your phone is on an older Android version, so this is a hard OS limit — root doesn\'t change it, and it will never work here. Turn on the phone\'s hotspot yourself instead; VPSH will detect it automatically.

VPSH shares your phone\'s internet with other devices over USB tethering or a Wi‑Fi hotspot — either as a full transparent VPN share (needs root) or as a local proxy (no root needed). BatProxy is a separate, second way to get online: it tunnels your own device\'s traffic through Cloudflare Workers, useful when your regular connection is blocked or unreliable.
Proxy mode — share your VPN with other devices, no root required
Full mode — transparent NAT sharing for rooted devices
BatProxy — tunnels the whole device through Cloudflare Workers, acting as its own VPN
Fully bilingual — English and Persian, switchable anytime from Settings
Kill-switch, health checks, and auto-restart so a dropped VPN never silently leaks

The main screen. \"Sharing mode\" switches between Proxy and Full (Full is greyed out without root). \"Start sharing / Stop sharing\" turns the foreground service on or off — once it\'s on, a persistent notification with its own Stop button lets you turn it off without opening the app again. Below that, the current public IP and exit country/flag are shown and refreshed every 5 seconds. The QR button next to Start shows the phone\'s IP, HTTP/SOCKS5 ports, and login (if you turned on authentication) as a scannable code. Stat chips show connected clients and traffic, and the device list lets you rename, rate-limit, or block each connected client. A blocked device is dropped immediately and disappears from the connected list, but it stays listed in a separate \"Blocked devices\" section below — with an Unblock button — so it can always be un-blocked later, even after it\'s no longer connected.

A dedicated tab for the hotspot itself, separate from sharing. The Dashboard\'s block only refuses the sharing proxy — a blocked device can still join the hotspot and reach other things on it. This tab bans by MAC address instead, right at the hotspot interface, so a banned device can\'t get anywhere through it at all — in Proxy or Full mode, or even with sharing stopped. It lists every device currently on the hotspot (from the system\'s neighbor table) with a Ban button, and a separate \"Banned from hotspot\" list with Unban, so past bans stay manageable even after the device disconnects. Needs root.

Connect / Disconnect turns the Cloudflare Workers tunnel on or off. The worker list is where you add or remove worker URLs and passwords; changing it while connected requires a reconnect. The live dashboard (Active / Total / OK / Fail) shows each worker\'s health — healthy, recovering, or cooling down after failures.

HTTP and SOCKS5 ports, optional username/password, health‑check interval, network interface overrides, the proxy‑mode kill‑switch (pauses sharing if the phone\'s VPN drops), chaining through another local proxy (for VLESS/VMess/Shadowsocks clients), and the language switcher.
A live feed of client connects/disconnects, proxy errors, and automatic restarts triggered by the health monitor (up to 5 attempts before it gives up).

No root needed. An HTTP proxy (and optional SOCKS5 proxy) runs on the phone; other devices must manually enter the phone\'s IP and port in their own proxy settings — only traffic that goes through that proxy is shared.

Needs root (Magisk or similar). Uses iptables/NAT to share the phone\'s entire active VPN with the tethering/hotspot interface — connected devices need zero configuration, and all of their traffic is covered.

In Proxy mode, other devices need their proxy settings configured manually. These two scripts do that automatically — enter the phone\'s IP/port (or scan for it) and they set up the system proxy, test the connection, and can save it as a profile for next time.
